The OTG port powers accessories like pads, drives and network adapters

Turn this on to reach the console from a computer through the OTG port: file transfer (MTP) or photo transfer (PTP), and adb once USB debugging is on in Developer options.

While it is on, accessories plugged into the OTG port don't work. The console always starts with it off, a restart switches the port back to accessories.

Some consoles don't wire the port for this. If the computer sees nothing with a good data cable, the console can't do it.

Never turn this on if your console has Wi-Fi built in, such as the R36XX. Those consoles use this same USB port for their Wi-Fi.

Never use this while the console is charging from its other port. Unplug the charger first. If a charger is plugged in while this is on, the port switches back to accessories right away.

Don\'t turn this on if your console has Wi-Fi built in, such as the R36XX. Those consoles use this same USB port for their Wi-Fi. Wi-Fi stops working, may not come back until you restart, and other things can go wrong.\n\nMost R36S consoles have no Wi-Fi built in. On those, this is safe.

Trade and battle in Game Boy games over the wired network.

1. On the first console choose this preset and Start. It is the USB device and network host, 192.168.36.1. Keep the second in Accessories/USB host mode; use a data cable and an OTG adapter on that side if needed. The second receives 192.168.36.2.

2. Start RetroArch on both, with matching core versions and compatible games. Back up each save and use separate saves. For GB/GBC, the bundled Gambatte supports its own network link: Quick Menu → Core Options → GB Link, show link settings, choose Network Server on .1 and Network Client on .2; set the client server IP digits to 192.168.36.1 and use the same port. Restart content after changing options. Leave ordinary RetroArch netplay off for this core.

3. For GBA, bundled gpSP uses RetroArch packet netplay. Set Core Options → Link Cable Connectivity to the appropriate cable mode (e.g. trading in Pokemon games) or wireless adapter mode on both; close and reload content. On .1 choose Netplay → Start Netplay Host; on .2 choose Connect to Netplay Host, 192.168.36.1, port 55435. Public announcement and relay are unnecessary.

SameBoy and TGB Dual are not bundled; their local dual-game modes do not automatically link two separate saves over ordinary netplay. Bundled mGBA does not provide this path. Core/game compatibility varies. Choose the core and content in RetroArch; this page does not replace saves or edit its configuration.

Stream PC games over the USB network instead of Wi-Fi. Moonlight is bundled with this ROM.

1. Install and configure Sunshine on the PC (sunshine-stream.org), add your games and allow its streaming ports on this local network in the PC firewall.

2. Start Network link here, then connect the PC as USB host. The console is 192.168.36.1; DHCP gives the PC 192.168.36.2 with no gateway or internet sharing. Use NCM on current systems, or Advanced → RNDIS on older Windows.

3. Open Moonlight, add the host manually as 192.168.36.2 and pair using the PIN in Sunshine. If the PC uses another address, enter that address instead. Select a game; Moonlight sends the console’s own buttons to the PC. No USB controller function is needed.

Start at 640×480, 60 fps, H.264 and 5–10 Mbps. Enable hardware decoding if available and reduce bitrate or frame rate if decoding lags. Turn Wi-Fi off for the first test to confirm the cable route. Keep the display on for streaming. Use the USB session notification to return here, or hold Select+Start to stop the link.
Start the wired network without opening an app.
The app is unavailable. Enable it in the app installer; Moonlight is also available from F-Droid (moonlight-stream.org).

Send overlapping sounds to the PC microphone through the sound card. Twelve examples are included. Add WAV/OGG/MP3 files to EASYROMS/soundboard (up to 8 MB and 10 seconds each; simple Latin filenames). The base console has no fitted microphone. Optional live input is offered when a microphone input is reported; enable it only with a fitted mic or headset. Works with the display off.

Up to %1$d GB available after reserving 1 GB. Sizes use 1 GB = 1024 × 1024 × 1024 bytes; maximum 1024 GB.
FAT32: widest compatibility with TVs, car stereos and consoles; individual files must be smaller than 4 GB.
exFAT: large files on modern Windows, macOS and Linux systems.
NTFS: large files, mainly for Windows PCs.
ext4: native Linux storage; Windows and most TVs cannot open it.
On FAT or exFAT, space is written out instead of reserved instantly. Large images take longer; keep the console powered.
Start with a letter or number. Use only English letters, numbers, spaces, dots, hyphens or underscores, up to 87 characters. No consecutive dots or trailing space or dot.
Use English letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens or underscores. FAT32 needs 1–11 characters and cannot start with a space; exFAT allows 15, NTFS 32 and ext4 16 characters.
Choose a whole number from 1 to 1024 GB that leaves at least 1 GB free on EASYROMS. Free space may have changed; refresh and try again.
EASYROMS is formatted as FAT32, which cannot hold a single image of 4 GB or larger. Choose a smaller image or use an exFAT card.
